identity.mechanic:
**Where the mechanic comes from:** Dominion's Band of Misfits and Overlord, cards you play as a copy of a cheaper card in the Supply without taking it.

**The twist.** In Bramble the shop is the Supply, and a copy lasts beyond one play. It stays on until the Changeling picks a new one. The tier cap stands in for Dominion's cost cap. And a changeling does take the original: the shop unit goes home to the pool, and the Board of Exchanges leaves a log in its place, because every swap is fair.

keywords.name: Guise
keywords.text:
While recruiting, once a turn, drag a shop unit onto this. It **wears** that unit: it gains the unit's text and tribe, keeping its own stats, its own text and the Changeling tribe. The guise stays until it wears another one, which replaces the old. It can wear a unit up to its own tier, or up to your tier minus 2, whichever is higher. The shop unit goes back to the pool, and a **Stock** takes its shop slot.

Guise rules:
- Worn text reads "this" as the Changeling.
- A worn "When played" does not trigger: the Changeling is already in play. Glamour-Weaver changes that.
- A worn unit's tribe counts for every tribe card and tribe bonus, so a Changeling in an Ooze guise is an Ooze.
- A golden Changeling wears golden text. That follows the triple rule, since the worn text is part of its text.
- A Changeling loses its guise when it makes a triple.
- **What counts as a wear.** Every guise a Changeling you own puts on while recruiting counts for cards that say "wears a unit" or count guises: Guise, a Stock bought under the Alder Whittler or Wicker Moll, and Inside-Out Tod's sales. Guises put on in a fight don't.
- **Wearing a Changeling** copies only its own printed text, never the guises it wears.
- **A guise put on at Start of Combat** fires its own Start of Combat text at once, right after the effect that gave it. A guise gained that way can't put on another guise this fight.
**Stock (token).** A Changeling, 0/3, Tier 1. It sits in the shop and costs 1 gold. No text, but it remembers the unit it replaced; it can wear that unit, at most once. It leaves when the shop refreshes, unless the shop is frozen. It's Created, so it sells for 0. Stocks never make triples.

identity.plays:
**How it plays.** A Changeling board is never quite the same twice. Each Recruit Phase you look at the shop as a menu of texts, not of bodies. Do you buy that Bog unit, or let your Foundling wear its Mire and leave a 1-gold Stock behind? Refresh and Freeze become ways to choose what your units *become*.

The tribe brings few stats of its own. It brings three levers:
- **Who** wears: Guise units, and later Stocks.
- **What** they may wear: tier raisers, wearing your own board, wearing what you sell, wearing the enemy.
- **Payoffs** for wearing often, and for wearing many tribes at once.

Its strength comes from whatever the other four tribes put in the shop. That gives Johnny an endless list of misuses: a Changeling that is an Ooze and a Bird at once, a mirror-backwards Pass, a Stock that eats like an Ooze, a second copy of your own carry's text.

units.name: Ant-Nest Grub

units.golden: 2/4. Guise. When this wears a unit: gain +2/+2 permanently.

units.name: Pip Unlike
units.text: Guise. Its guise is mirror-backwards: left and right swap in the worn text. (A worn Pass goes to your leftmost other unit.)

units.name: Knowe Nursemaid
units.text: When a Changeling you own wears a unit: give it +1/+1 permanently.

units.name: Leaf-Gold Pedlar
units.text: Once a turn, when a Changeling you own wears a unit: gain 1 gold.

units.name: Porter of the Seven Doors
units.text: Your Changelings can wear units 1 tier above their own.

units.name: Hoverfly Guest
units.text: Guise. Start of Combat: this also wears the enemy across it this fight, ignoring tier. That guise's Start of Combat text fires at once.
units.golden: 6/8. Same, and both guises are golden text.

units.name: Bee Orchid
units.text: End of Turn: give each Changeling you own that wears a unit +1/+1 permanently.

units.name: Alder Whittler
units.text: Once a turn, when you buy a Stock: it wears the unit it replaced (up to Tier 3).

units.name: Tam Twice
units.text: Guise. It can also wear a unit you own. That unit stays and leaves no Stock. A Changeling worn this way gives only its own text, not its guises.

units.name: Michaelmas Mummers
units.text: End of Turn: for each different tribe your Changelings wear, give another random Changeling +2/+2 permanently.

units.name: Glamour-Weaver
units.text: Once a turn, when a Changeling you own wears a unit: that unit's "When played" text triggers for it.

units.name: Inside-Out Tod
units.text: Guise. When you sell a unit: this may wear it, ignoring tier. If it does, it gains half that unit's stats permanently.
units.golden: 8/10. Same, wearing golden text, and gains all of that unit's stats.

units.name: Wicker Moll
units.text: When you buy a Stock: it wears the unit it replaced (up to Tier 5) and gains +3/+3 permanently.

units.name: Coat-Peg Steward
units.text: When another Changeling you own dies: this also wears its guises this fight, stacking with any it already has, and gains +4/+4.

units.name: Grandfer Acorn
units.text: Guise. This keeps up to 3 guises at once; a 4th sheds the oldest.

units.name: The Lady Under the Hill
units.text: Guise. Your other Changelings wear golden text.
units.golden: 14/14. Guise. Your Changelings, this one included, wear golden text, and the numbers in their worn text are doubled once more.

units.name: Bettie Underhill
units.text: End of Turn: give your Changelings +1/+1 permanently for each guise your Changelings put on this turn.

units.name: Penny Second
units.text: Start of Combat: each Changeling in your front row wears the enemy across it this fight, ignoring tier, and that enemy loses its text this fight. Those guises' Start of Combat texts fire at once.

extras.name: Stock

builds.name: A. The Masquerade (wear many tribes).
builds.text: Use Foundling, Grub and Pip early, then the Porter, Bee Orchid and Michaelmas Mummers. Aim for four or five Guise units each wearing a different tribe. The Nursemaid and Bee Orchid grow every wearer, and the Mummers grow more with each new tribe. Each Changeling also picks up other tribes' bonuses: a Changeling in a Hedgerow guise gets Harvest Supper's Hedgerow bonus. This is the most flexible build and the easiest to pivot from.

builds.name: B. The Stock Exchange.
builds.text: Use the Leaf-Gold Pedlar and Alder Whittler, then Wicker Moll and Bettie. Every guise leaves a Stock, and under Moll every Stock is a 3/6 for 1 gold that wears the unit it replaced. One shop unit becomes two copies of its text, and the board fills with Changelings for Bettie to grow. The limits are board space and how many Guise actions you have each turn.

builds.name: C. The Impostor Does It Better (copy your carry).
builds.text: Use Tam Twice, Glamour-Weaver, Grandfer Acorn and Inside-Out Tod, finished by the Lady. Pick one strong text, say another tribe's T4–T5 buffer or combat engine you already own. Tam wears it from your board. Grandfer stacks it with two other texts. Tod wears whatever you sell, including a golden you've outgrown, and takes half its stats. With the Lady, every copy is golden.

builds.name: D. Swap Noticed Too Late (fight-time copies).
builds.text: Use the Hoverfly Guest, then Coat-Peg Steward and Penny Second. Read your next opponent's last board and put Changelings across their best units. The Hoverfly copies the enemy across it. Penny copies the enemy units across your front row and wipes their text, which hard-counters text-heavy carries. The Steward gathers the guises of fallen Changelings as the fight goes on.

builds.name: E. The Turnover (sell to wear).
builds.text: Use Inside-Out Tod with the Knowe Nursemaid, then Bettie Underhill. Every unit you sell can be a wear: Tod takes its text and half its stats, the Nursemaid grows Tod, and each sale adds a Bettie stack at End of Turn. Buy a 1-gold Stock or a 3-gold shop unit just to sell it. Gold is the only limit, so this is the late-game gold sink.

builds.name: In a lobby.
builds.text: The Changelings are parasites by design. Wearing takes nothing from the pool (the worn unit goes back), so they don't starve other players, but they're only as good as the other tribes' texts in their shop. They mix best with texts that work on any body: Bog units' Mire and Bitter, Hunters' Quarry and Pack, Ooze Eat and Belly. "Your Fairies" texts are weak in a guise unless you own Fairies. The natural mid-game shape is one real tribe plus Changelings in its guises, for example three Oozes and three Ooze-guised Changelings.

risks: **Two layers of text on one card** (up to four on Grandfer). The UI must show the guise clearly, say as a small portrait badge you tap to read, or the tribe is unreadable.

**The tier cap could starve early Guise units late.** v2 adopts the fallback: a Changeling can always wear up to your tier minus 2, so a Foundling at Tier 6 wears Tier 4 units. The Porter still lifts a Changeling's own cap by one.
**Traps.** Wearing "your Birds get..." with no Birds does nothing. That's honest, but new players will fall into it. The tutorial should cover it, not the card.
**Stock efficiency under Wicker Moll** may be too strong: 1 gold for a 3/6 carrying up to Tier 5 text. If so, Stocks cost 2 under Moll, or Moll's Stocks lose the +3/+3.
**Penny Second's text wipe** can feel unfair to the opponent, since four enemy texts are gone at Start of Combat. Fallback: she copies without wiping, and the wipe goes only on her golden.

**Multiplier stacking.** Grandfer wearing three Glamour-Weavers under a golden Lady gives many free When-played triggers a turn. Each source is once or twice a turn, so growth is bounded and linear, not runaway. But the high roll is very high, so test it.

**Tod and Bettie turn gold into stats.** Every sale under Tod is a wear, so each 1–2 gold spent on buy-and-sell adds a Bettie stack. It's bounded by gold, not looped, but test the late-game high roll.
**Stocks never triple** is an exception to a global rule. It's needed: otherwise three 1-gold Stocks buy a Discover.

**Open rules questions,** with proposals: a worn "Once a turn" counter belongs to the Changeling and doesn't reset on re-wearing; a guise survives Fly South; wearing a Shy Fairy makes the Changeling Shy.

**Identity hole.** With few stats of its own, the tribe can feel like "other tribes, but worse bodies". The payoffs (Nursemaid, Bee Orchid, Mummers, Bettie) have to make wearing often clearly better than buying the original.

tier_check.note: Foundling is a 4-stat body plus a Tier 1 text, a normal Tier 1; late it wears up to your tier minus 2. Grub grows 2 stats a turn (0.5 body against ~0.4), slightly over on purpose because it only grows if it takes a new guise each turn.
6-stat bodies. Nursemaid gives about 6 stats a turn with three wearers (1 body, top of range). Pedlar's 1 gold a turn is a third of a unit. Pip is a body plus a Tier 2 text.

7-stat bodies. Bee Orchid gives about 8 stats a turn with four wearers (1.1 against ~0.8), about 2 bodies once Moll's Stocks join: over on purpose, as the reason to stack wearers. Hoverfly's enemy copy is about 1–1.4 bodies in fight, swingy. Porter and Whittler are enablers with low stats.
Mummers give 12 stats a turn with three tribes worn (1.4 against ~1.3). Weaver gives one free When-played a turn, about 1–2 bodies. Tod's sale gain is once, about 2 bodies. Tam is the enabler.

Moll gives about 3 Stocks a turn at 9 stats plus their texts, about 2.5 bodies plus text, near the top of range. Steward gives 24–32 stats plus texts, under the ~4 in-fight target but with uncapped texts. Grandfer triples one body's text.

Bettie gives about 56 stats a turn with 4 guises and 7 Changelings (~4 bodies, on target). The Lady doubles every worn text. Penny is well over 6 bodies against a text-heavy board and little against a vanilla one, a deliberate swing. The Lady's golden reaches ×4 on worn numbers, the top of the golden ceiling, on purpose.

rationale: **I started from Band of Misfits** because "becomes what it replaces" is the seed, and the shop is a natural Supply to copy from.
**The shop unit is taken and a Stock is left** to make the copy cost something you can see (that unit is no longer for sale) and to put the folklore's stock on the board.
**I capped by tier, not cost.** Bramble units all cost 3, so tier is the only lever, and it lets the tier raisers form a ladder.
**The worn tribe counts for other tribes' cards and bonuses.** That interweaving across tribes is what Johnny asked for.
**The worn text adds to the Changeling's own text** so every Changeling keeps its own small job and the payoffs have something to hook on.
**Each Changeling wears once a turn.** That bounds every engine linearly and keeps the runaway check simple.
**I built the four levers:** who wears, what can be worn (own board, sold units, enemies, higher tiers), how often, and how many tribes.
**Stocks got a ladder:** the Whittler (once a turn, up to Tier 3), then Moll (every Stock, up to Tier 5). It follows rule of thumb 3: more recipients, not bigger numbers.
**The fight-time copy got a ladder too:** the Hoverfly copies one enemy, and Penny copies and wipes up to four.
**Goldens wear golden text** because it follows the triple rule anyway, and it gives the Lady a doubling capstone.
**Stocks don't triple.** I cut the 3-gold Discover loop rather than price it.
**Names and lore came last,** fitted to each job: Pip's mirror copies, Tam's family, Penny turning the duchess away, Moll's stocks, and Bettie's ledger as the payoff for wearing often.

changes.what: Guise rules say what counts as a wear, what wearing a Changeling copies, when Start of Combat guises fire; always wears up to tier minus 2.
changes.why: Reviewers couldn't tell which wears feed payoffs or when fight guises fire; late Tier 1 wearers had nothing to wear.

changes.what: Mirror now swaps only left and right, with a worked example on the card.
changes.why: Four swaps at once couldn't be read; left-right is the joke and reads instantly.

changes.what: Says the worn enemy's Start of Combat text fires at once.
changes.why: It was unclear whether a guise taken at Start of Combat fires that fight.

changes.what: Says a Changeling worn by Tam gives only its own text, not its guises.
changes.why: Unclear whether Tam copied Grandfer's three guises along with its text.

changes.what: Tod may wear a sold unit instead of always wearing it; stat gain comes only with the wear.
changes.why: Forced re-wears stripped guises you wanted; the choice keeps the sell engine readable.

changes.what: Now a buy trigger: a bought Stock wears its replaced unit and gains +3/+3 permanently.
changes.why: Says when Moll's Stocks wear, so they clearly count as wears for the payoffs.

changes.what: Gathered guises now stack this fight, with any the Steward already has.
changes.why: It was unclear whether each fallen Changeling's guise stacked or replaced the last.

changes.what: Counts every guise your Changelings put on together, not each Changeling's own.
changes.why: The text read two ways; Stock and Tod wears now clearly count, bounded by gold.

changes.what: Says the front-row guises' Start of Combat texts fire at once.
changes.why: Same timing question as the Hoverfly Guest.

changes.what: A Stock remembers the unit it replaced and can wear it at most once.
changes.why: Moll and the Whittler both need that memory; once stops a double-counted wear.
